quickSummary: Cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes) possess placoid scales, ventral mouths, lack operculums/swim bladders, and have pelvic claspers with internal fertilization. Bony fishes (Osteichthyes) possess cycloid/ctenoid scales, terminal mouths, operculums, and hydrostatic swim bladders.

summaryBox.takeaway: Critical contrasts: Sharks lack swim bladders and operculums (exposed gill slits) and use pelvic claspers for internal fertilization; Bony fishes have swim bladders and operculums.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 Comprehensive Comparative Matrix of Fishes
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Comprehensive Comparative Matrix of Fishes
conceptBreakdown.content:
| Diagnostic Trait | Class Chondrichthyes (Cartilaginous) | Class Osteichthyes (Bony) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Habitat** | Exclusively **marine** | Marine AND Freshwater ecosystems |
| **Endoskeleton** | Persistent **Cartilaginous** endoskeleton | **Bony** endoskeleton |
| **Mouth Position** | **Ventral** | Mostly **Terminal** |
| **Exoskeletal Scales** | Tough skin covered by **Placoid Scales** (modified teeth directed posteriorly) | Skin covered by **Cycloid** or **Ctenoid Scales** |
| **Gill Slits & Operculum** | $5\text{--}7\text{ pairs}$ of gill slits; **Operculum ABSENT** (except *Chimaera*) | $4\text{ pairs}$ of gills; covered by a bony **Operculum** on each side |
| **Swim / Air Bladder** | **ABSENT**; must swim continuously to avoid sinking | **PRESENT**; regulates buoyancy hydrostatically |
| **Intestinal Spiral Valve** | Contains a spiral fold (**Typhlosole / Scroll Valve**) to increase absorptive area | Scroll valve absent; longer intestine |
| **Fertilization & Reproduction** | Internal fertilization; males possess **Pelvic Claspers**; mostly **Viviparous** | External fertilization; claspers absent; mostly **Oviparous** |
| **Excretory Waste** | **Ureotelic** (retains high urea in blood for osmoregulation) | **Ammonotelic** (freshwater) or Ureotelic (marine) |
| **Specialized Organs** | Electric Organs (*Torpedo*); Poison Stings (*Trygon*); **Ampullae of Lorenzini** (electroreceptors) | Well-developed Lateral Line System detecting hydrodynamic vibrations |
| **Representative Taxa** | *Scoliodon* (dogfish), *Pristis* (sawfish), *Carcharodon* (great white shark), *Trygon* | *Exocoetus* (flying fish), *Hippocampus* (sea horse), *Labeo*, *Catla*, *Clarias*, *Betta* |
